observations.text: SP, due to insufficient knowledge of the formation take off procedure, did not apply the essential factors for placing No2 on the correct side and could not complete the lineup and run-up sequence without assistance. The IP directed the lineup on the assigned half of the runway and set part of the power, while lateral displacement from the assigned runway centerline reference reached 15 ft and rotation was initiated 6 knots below the calculated take off airspeed. The landing gear retraction command was given without confirming that No2 was safely airborne, with the result that the IP cancelled the call and directed the correct sequence. Further study of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and of the SOP formation take off sequence is required.

SP performed the formation take off within the standards required for the Training Section, completing the sequence after the IP's verbal prompts for the wind check and for the side assignment of No2. Take off airspeed reached +10 knots over the calculated value and lateral displacement reached 10 ft from the assigned runway centerline reference, both recognized and corrected with delay. No2 was monitored during the roll and the landing gear retraction command was given only after No2 was confirmed safely airborne. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independence in the lineup and in the rotation sequence, without IP prompting, is expected to improve in the next sortie.

SP determined the correct side for No2 from the wind and the departure direction and flew the formation take off with no IP prompts on the sequence. Minor deviations of +7 knots on take off airspeed and 8 ft from the assigned runway centerline reference were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. No2 was effectively monitored throughout the roll and the landing gear retraction command followed the confirmation that No2 was safely airborne. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied all the essential factors to place No2 on the correct side, held the assigned runway centerline reference within 4 ft and rotated within +4 knots of the calculated take off airspeed. Brake release, power application and run-up were executed accurately and rapidly, in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the SOPs, without IP prompts. Monitoring of No2 was continuous and the landing gear retraction command was given immediately after No2 was confirmed safely airborne. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the formation take off with exceptional precision, placing No2 on the correct side after full consideration of the wind and of the departure direction. Lateral displacement from the assigned runway centerline reference remained within 2 ft and take off airspeed was held within +1 knot of the calculated value through rotation. Monitoring of No2 was uninterrupted and the landing gear retraction command was timed exactly to the confirmation that No2 was safely airborne. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor cockpit indication while the aircraft state went unmonitored, did not hold the assigned runway centerline reference during the roll and did not monitor No2. Lateral displacement reached 16 ft and take off airspeed was allowed to exceed the calculated value by 13 knots before the IP took the controls to reestablish the lineup. The landing gear retraction command was issued without confirming that No2 was safely airborne, so the IP had to direct the remainder of the sequence.

SP, due to a non-standardized power application technique at brake release, did not match the briefed acceleration and did not keep No2 in view on the correct side during the roll. Take off airspeed reached the +10 knot limit over the calculated value and lateral displacement reached 10 ft from the assigned runway centerline reference, with the result that the maneuver was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts and both deviations were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP executed the formation take off within the desired standards for the Training Section, placing No2 on the correct side and monitoring it through rotation. Deviations of +7 knots on take off airspeed and 8 ft from the assigned runway centerline reference were twice self-corrected without IP intervention, and the landing gear retraction command followed the confirmation that No2 was safely airborne. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a steadier directional reference during the first half of the roll is expected to improve consistency.

SP applied the wind and departure factors correctly to place No2 on the correct side and executed the formation take off accurately and rapidly, in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the SOPs. The assigned runway centerline reference was held within 4 ft and take off airspeed within +3 knots of the calculated value, with no IP prompts. No2 was effectively monitored during the entire maneuver and the landing gear retraction command followed the immediate confirmation that No2 was safely airborne. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional accuracy in the formation take off, holding the assigned runway centerline reference within 2 ft and take off airspeed within +1 knot of the calculated value. All the essential factors were taken into consideration to place No2 on the correct side, and monitoring of No2 continued uninterrupted from brake release to the landing gear retraction command. Timing and directional control were above the levels desired at this point of the syllabus. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incomplete lineup technique on the assigned half of the runway, did not establish the correct directional reference before brake release and did not apply the factors for placing No2 on the correct side. Lateral displacement reached 17 ft from the assigned runway centerline reference and rotation was initiated 5 knots below the calculated take off airspeed, with the result that the IP took the controls during the roll. The landing gear retraction command was given before No2 was confirmed safely airborne and had to be corrected by the IP.

SP, due to workload distribution that left the take off roll, the formation calls and the monitoring of No2 attempted at the same time, did not hold the assigned runway centerline reference and did not check No2 before the landing gear retraction command. Take off airspeed reached the +10 knot limit over the calculated value and lateral displacement reached 10 ft, both recognized and corrected with delay after the IP's verbal prompts. The maneuver was completed without IP intervention on the controls, but only after those prompts.

SP, due to a late directional correction after brake release, allowed the A/C to drift from the assigned runway centerline reference and delayed the visual check of No2. Lateral displacement reached 8 ft and take off airspeed +7 knots over the calculated value, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. The landing gear retraction command was given after confirming that No2 was safely airborne.

SP performed the formation take off within the desired standards, holding the assigned runway centerline reference within 5 ft and take off airspeed within +5 knots of the calculated value. All the essential factors were taken into consideration to place No2 on the correct side, although the monitoring of No2 was momentarily interrupted during rotation. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a continuous visual scan of No2 from rotation through landing gear retraction is expected to improve.

SP executed the formation take off with exceptional precision, holding the assigned runway centerline reference within 2 ft and take off airspeed within +1 knot of the calculated value. The side assignment for No2 accounted for the wind, the departure direction and the obstacle considerations of the briefed departure, and No2 was monitored continuously from brake release onward. The landing gear retraction command was given at the exact moment No2 was confirmed safely airborne. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient knowledge of the interval take off spacing procedure, did not establish the briefed interval and could not complete the departure sequence without assistance. The IP directed the timing of brake release and set part of the power, while lateral displacement reached 15 ft from the runway centerline and rotation was initiated 5 knots below the calculated take off airspeed. No2 was not monitored after brake release and the landing gear retraction command was given without confirmation that No2 was safely airborne, with the result that the IP took over the formation calls. Further study of the SOP interval take off procedure is required.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic during a critical phase of flight, did not hold the runway centerline within the required tolerance and did not check that No2 was safely airborne before the landing gear retraction command. Take off airspeed reached the +10 knot limit over the calculated value and lateral displacement reached 10 ft, both recognized and corrected with delay after the IP's verbal prompts. The interval take off was completed without IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to a late rotation input at the calculated take off airspeed, exceeded the reference speed and allowed a lateral drift during the second half of the roll. Take off airspeed reached +7 knots over the calculated value and displacement from the runway centerline reached 8 ft, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. The briefed interval was established, No2 was monitored during its roll and the landing gear retraction command followed the confirmation that No2 was safely airborne.

SP executed the interval take off within the desired standards, holding the runway centerline within 5 ft and take off airspeed within +5 knots of the calculated value. The briefed interval was met and No2 was monitored after brake release, although the confirmation that No2 was safely airborne preceded the landing gear retraction command by a very short margin. Marginal performance for the Training Section - clearer timing between the confirmation of No2 airborne and the gear command is expected to improve.

SP executed the interval take off with exceptional precision, holding the runway centerline within 2 ft and take off airspeed within +1 knot of the calculated value. The briefed interval was established exactly, all the essential factors were applied to place No2 on the correct side for the rejoin, and No2 was monitored continuously until confirmed safely airborne. The landing gear retraction command was given only after that confirmation and without any IP prompt. Above end of block MIF achieved.
